title: Mariner Logistics evaluation pack and acceptance criteria
content:
Overview:
This document is the customer-specific evaluation pack for Mariner Logistics (beta integration). Purpose: provide pinned prompts, private dataset descriptors, acceptance criteria, regression test suites, and sign-off flow for model onboarding into Redwood Dedicated for Mariner’s operational chat and manifest-assistant features. This is a working deliverable intended to be iterated during the QA and customer validation phase.

Scope and goals:
- Scope: conversational routing + manifest parsing + short-answer troubleshooting for dock operators. Not in scope: full invoicing automation, long-form SLA negotiation.
- Primary success criteria: production-quality responses for manifest extraction and short operational queries with latency and cost within agreed SLOs.

Private datasets (access-controlled):
- mariner_manifests_q4_2024.csv (3,240 manifests; sanitized PII; shipping identifiers retained) — canonical manifest examples used to generate extraction gold labels.
- mariner_chat_logs_sample_2024.jsonl (8,100 messages, redacted operator names) — used for conversational turn-taking and context-length tests.
- manifest_edgecases.xlsx (approx 220 rows) — intentionally malformed manifests (missing fields, split lines, nonstandard units).
Data access notes:
- All files live in the Mariner S3 bucket under s3://mariner-prod/onboarding/redwood-inference/ and are accessible via short-lived credentials created per-engagement.
- Data steward: Mariner contact (Daniel Ko) holds final approval for any additional data extracts.
- Security: Private datasets must not be exported outside of Redwood Dedicated endpoints; training is disallowed; only evaluation queries against a pinned model snapshot.

Evaluation harness and metrics (how we measure):
- Functional metrics (primary):
  - Extraction F1: token-level match on manifest fields (expected threshold >= 0.92 for primary fields: origin_port, destination_port, weight, item_count).
  - Field completeness: percentage of manifests where all required fields are present in model output (threshold >= 0.90).
- Quality metrics (secondary):
  - Hallucination rate: % of answers with fabricated shipment identifiers or dates (threshold <= 1.5%).
  - Precision on numeric fields: abs(error) <= 2% for weights, counts.
- Operational metrics:
  - 95th percentile latency (generate API): <= 240ms for short prompts; <= 700ms for full manifest extraction under standard load.
  - Cost per 1K tokens and per call tracked vs baseline.
- Safety/Privacy checks:
  - No leaked PII in outputs (automated regex + manual review).
  - Auditable trace: every eval run links to dataset snapshot id and model version.

Pinned prompt set (do not change without applied-ml sign-off):
1) Manifest-extract-v1: System: "You are a precise manifest extractor. Return JSON with keys: origin_port, destination_port, total_weight_kg, total_items, manifest_id. If a field is missing, return null."
   - Example user input: "MANIFEST: M-9932
ORIGIN: Longview Port
DEST: Tacoma
WEIGHT: 4,200 kg
ITEMS: 52
"
   - Expected output (gold): {"manifest_id":"M-9932","origin_port":"Longview Port","destination_port":"Tacoma","total_weight_kg":4200,"total_items":52}
   - Accept tolerance: numeric types must parse to integer/float; string normalization allowed for common abbreviations.
2) Short-troubleshoot-v1: System: "You are a logistic operations assistant. Answer briefly (<= 2 sentences) and reference manifest ids when relevant."
   - Prompt example: "Why was M-417 delayed?" (context includes last 3 events in timeline).
   - Expected: concise reasoning pointing to event (e.g., "Delay due to customs hold on 2024-11-03, document mismatch").
3) Ambiguity-resolve-v1: System: "When user query is ambiguous about which manifest, ask one clarifying question."
   - Example: user: "Status of the shipment to Tacoma?"
   - Expected: question to disambiguate which manifest.

Regression tests and gold set management:
- Golden set: 320 manifests selected from mariner_manifests_q4_2024 representing common, edge, and adversarial cases. Each record includes a golden extraction output file (golden_extracts_v1.jsonl).
- Regression runs: run against every model snapshot candidate. A snapshot fails the gate if: extraction F1 drops by >1.5 absolute points vs baseline snapshot OR hallucination rate increases by >0.75%.
- Scheduled regression cadence: nightly against baseline (canary snapshot) and pre-rollout full run (all 320) for any candidate marked for canary.
- Manual review bucket: any outputs flagged by the automated checker (regex mismatch, numeric parse failure, PII triggers) are reviewed by an applied-ml engineer within 24 hours.

Acceptance thresholds (final sign-off criteria):
- Functional: Extraction F1 >= 0.92 and field completeness >=0.90 across full golden set.
- Quality: Hallucination <= 1.5% and numeric precision within 2% for at least 98% of numeric fields.
- Performance: p95 latency <= 240ms (short prompts) and <=700ms (full manifest under concurrency 8).
- Stability: No regression failures in 3 consecutive nightly runs; memory/leak checks show <2% variance in steady-state GPU memory over 24h.
- Security: No PII leakage findings in audits; data access logs verified for the evaluation period.

Sign-off flow (roles and responsibilities):
- Applied ML owner (Aisha Patel): validates metrics, oversees regression, signs functional acceptance.
- SRE/Infra rep (Marcus Chen): validates performance metrics, deployment readiness, autoscaling configs.
- Customer Success (Lina Garcia): coordinates customer validation and operational readiness with Mariner.
- Security/compliance reviewer (Omar Voss): approves data access controls and audit evidence.
Sign-off steps:
1) Complete full golden run and attach artifact links to JIRA (JIRA-ML-3421).
2) SRE smoke test in staging (latency and resource checks).
3) Customer validation window (48h) — Mariner runs curated user scenarios and signs customer acceptance sheet.
4) Final internal sign-off: all four roles confirm via JIRA comment and close the onboarding checklist.

Rollout plan (canary -> ramp -> GA):
- Canary (step 0): 2% of production traffic routed to new model variant in Dedicated with circuit-breaker (error rate threshold 3x baseline). Monitor extraction F1 and hallucinations in real time.
- Ramp (step 1): 10% traffic for 24h if canary green.
- Ramp (step 2): 50% traffic for 48h with auto-roll-back on defined triggers (see monitoring signals).
- GA: 100% after 7d stable behavior.
Monitoring signals and rollback triggers:
- Instant rollback if error rate > 5% absolute OR hallucination spike +2% absolute over baseline in any 1h window.
- Degraded-only rollback if p95 latency increases by >200ms sustained for 30m.
- Alerting: Slack channel #cs-mariner and PagerDuty route to on-call applied-ml engineer.

Known limitations and mitigations:
- Nonstandard units (lbs vs kg) occasionally mis-normalize: mitigation: preprocessing layer to canonicalize units before model input.
- Multi-manifest messages: extractor sometimes merges fields from multiple manifests — mitigation: add conversation-scoped manifest-id anchor and a post-parser consistency check.

Appendix: sample prompts and additional gold examples (short list)
- Prompt A (extraction): "RAW MANIFEST:
ID: M-1101
ORIGIN: Port of Oakland
DEST: Port of Seattle
WT: 2.3 tonnes
CNT: 11"
  Gold: origin_port="Port of Oakland"; destination_port="Port of Seattle"; total_weight_kg=2300; total_items=11
- Prompt B (ambiguous manifest ask): "I need ETA for the shipment to Seattle" (context: two open manifests to Seattle).
  Expected: clarifying question naming manifest ids.

Open questions / next steps:
- Confirm final golden-set selection with Mariner ops (assigned to Lina).
- Agree on log retention window for evaluation logs (customer prefference: 30 days).
- Determine whether Mariner wants automated correction suggestions for numeric parsing errors (product decision).

Notes to reviewers: this is a working pack; do not change pinned prompts without updating golden tests and notifying the customer. Add any new gold records under golden_extracts_v2/ with author + date metadata.

Document history:
- 2025-11-12: initial draft by Aisha Patel
- 2025-12-05: added regression gating rules (Marcus Chen)
- 2026-01-18: updated acceptance thresholds and rollout triggers (SRE feedback)
- 2026-02-24: customer validation window schedule added (Lina Garcia)
